# frostmoln_messaging_user (Resource)

Manages an application user on a managed messaging (LavinMQ) instance: an AMQP-only login with a password the platform generates. The user reaches nothing until a `frostmoln_messaging_permission` grants it a vhost.

Create and destroy wait until the platform has applied the change on the broker; the password is read once the user is `ready`, and again on every refresh. Operations on one instance run one at a time, so the provider serialises every vhost, user and permission change per instance. Destroying a user is refused while any permission still names it.

Import with `<instance_id>/<name>`; the import reads the password too.

**Authoritative scope** — who owns what on this resource, declared in `internal/scopedecl` and machine-checked against the schema.

**Create-immutable** — `instance_id`, `name`: a user is identified by its name on its instance, and the broker has no rename; changing either creates a new user with a new password.

**Observed, not enacted** — `password`: generated by the platform and re-read on every refresh while the user is ready.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An AMQP-only application user. The platform generates the password; it is
# read once the user is ready.
resource "frostmoln_messaging_user" "billing" {
  instance_id = frostmoln_messaging_instance.broker.id
  name        = "billing-app"
}

# The user reaches nothing until a frostmoln_messaging_permission grants it a
# vhost. Hand the connection URL to the application. The broker serves no TLS
# yet, so connect over plain AMQP from inside the instance's VPC:
output "billing_amqp_url" {
  sensitive = true
  value = format("amqp://%s:%s@%s:%d/%s", # pragma: allowlist secret
    frostmoln_messaging_user.billing.name,
    urlencode(frostmoln_messaging_user.billing.password),
    frostmoln_messaging_instance.broker.private_ip,
    frostmoln_messaging_instance.broker.port,
    frostmoln_messaging_vhost.orders.name,
  )
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The id of the `frostmoln_messaging_instance` the user lives on. Changing it creates the user on the other instance, with a new password, and deletes this one.
- `name` (String) The user's name, which is also its AMQP username: 1 to 64 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, unique on the instance regardless of case (`Orders` cannot be created while `orders` exists); a change in case is a different name. The instance's admin user, `guest` and `__direct` are refused. Changing it replaces the user and issues a new password.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the user was created.
- `failure_message` (String) The last failed change's reason in words, or null.
- `failure_reason` (String) The stable code of the user's last failed change (for example `IN_FLIGHT` or `BROKER_REFUSED`), or null. Every code but `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` means the broker was left unchanged.
- `id` (String) The user's Terraform id, `<instance_id>/<name>`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The user's AMQP password, generated by the platform and read once the user is `ready`. Null only while the platform could not serve it; the next refresh reads it. Stored in Terraform state in plaintext — `sensitive` redacts CLI output, not the state file. See the [Secrets in Terraform state](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/frostmoln/frostmoln/latest/docs/guides/state-and-secrets) guide.
- `status` (String) The user's status: `pending` while the platform applies a create, `ready`, `deleting`, or `error` when a create failed (the user is absent or its state unknown; the next apply deletes and re-creates it).
- `updated_at` (String) When the user last changed.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long the provider waits for the create operation to converge before giving up (e.g. "45m", "2h").
- `delete` (String) How long the provider waits for the delete to complete before giving up (e.g. "30m").
- `update` (String) How long the provider waits for an update (resize, in-place change) to converge before giving up (e.g. "30m").

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the composite ID {instance_id}/{name}. The import reads the
# user's password too.
terraform import frostmoln_messaging_user.billing mq_B352H9idUJP6jTWtom31nW/billing-app
```
